title: Ecosystem Security — The Shield capability model
mission: The horizontal security authority for the Ecosystem: defining security rules, reusable baselines, assurance semantics, and the evidence required to justify security claims.
currentState: The Shield is at an early foundation stage. Strong Room v1 is the only implemented reusable capability; all other status labels describe repository maturity, not ecosystem-wide deployment or compliance.

owns: canonical security controls and assessment semantics
reusable security baselines, including Strong Room
doesNotOwn: the canonical repository, service, or infrastructure inventory
application-specific configuration, authorization, threat models, or evidence
production runtime state or deployment operations
provider credentials, secrets, or identity enrollment material
operational responsibilities assigned to application, infrastructure, or service owners

productionAuthorization.rule: A human approval gate is required immediately before every production-impacting change.
productionAuthorization.prohibitedInference: Tests, checks, CI results, agents, and AI-generated recommendations are evidence inputs only and must never be treated as authorization.

statusModel.PLANNED: Intended capability with no maintained implementation or governing foundation yet.
statusModel.FOUNDATION: Canonical structure, semantics, or requirements exist, but the capability is not operational.
statusModel.PARTIAL: A bounded subset exists; uncovered scope remains explicit.
statusModel.IMPLEMENTED: A maintained Shield-owned capability exists for its stated scope; this does not prove adoption or effectiveness elsewhere.
statusModel.VERIFIED: Current evidence demonstrates the stated scope and provenance. Verification is bounded, dated, and never inferred from documentation.

actionabilityModel.ROADMAP: Informational architecture only; there is no operational action in the Shield.
actionabilityModel.GOVERNANCE: A Shield governance artifact or model can be used, but it is not an operational service.
actionabilityModel.AVAILABLE: A bounded Shield-owned reusable capability is available for adoption and independent verification.

assessmentStates.PASS: The scoped expected behavior was actually observed.
assessmentStates.FAIL: A performed assessment contradicted its expectation.
assessmentStates.BLOCKED: The assessment could not finish because a prerequisite, authorization, or access was missing.
assessmentStates.NOT_TESTED: No assessment attempt has been made.
assessmentStates.TECHNICALLY_UNAVAILABLE: The environment lacks the technical capability; record proof and coverage impact. This is not PASS.

integrationBoundaries.name: Ecosystem Framework / The DNA
integrationBoundaries.provides: ecosystem principles, governance context, and canonical cross-domain conventions
integrationBoundaries.shieldRelationship: The Shield specializes ecosystem rules into security requirements without duplicating the framework.

integrationBoundaries.name: Foundation Systems
integrationBoundaries.provides: shared platform and foundational service state
integrationBoundaries.shieldRelationship: The Shield defines security expectations and consumes scoped state or evidence through future integrations.

integrationBoundaries.name: Infrastructure
integrationBoundaries.provides: network, host, cloud, backup, and runtime state
integrationBoundaries.shieldRelationship: Infrastructure implements and operates its controls; the Shield defines requirements and assurance semantics.

integrationBoundaries.name: Core and Intelligence
integrationBoundaries.shieldRelationship: They adopt Shield controls and retain their own sensitive configuration, risks, and evidence.

integrationBoundaries.name: Ecosystem Control — The Brain
integrationBoundaries.provides: canonical ecosystem inventory, coordination, and presentation of ecosystem state
integrationBoundaries.shieldRelationship: Control may display security state, but it does not replace Shield authority or become the only alert path.

integrationBoundaries.name: Application and service repositories
integrationBoundaries.provides: implementation, populated configuration, deployment state, and application-specific evidence
integrationBoundaries.shieldRelationship: Applications reference the adopted Shield baseline and keep their populated configuration and evidence locally.

capabilities.name: Security Governance
capabilities.purpose: Establish accountable security ownership, decision authority, reviews, approvals, reporting, and assurance across the Ecosystem.
capabilities.scope: Principles; roles and responsibilities; policy, control, and risk ownership; decision and approval processes; periodic reviews; KPIs/KRIs; maturity and governance evidence.

capabilities.name: Security Policy Management
capabilities.purpose: Maintain an approved, versioned, owned, and reviewable catalogue of security policies.
capabilities.scope: Policy ID, owner, scope, effective date, version, review date, approval state, supersession, exceptions, linked standards, controls, and evidence.

capabilities.name: Common Security Standards / Baseline
capabilities.purpose: Define minimum machine-addressable security expectations that apply across the Ecosystem.
capabilities.scope: Secure defaults; authentication and authorization; least privilege; MFA/passkeys; encryption; TLS and headers; sessions; network exposure; proxies and firewalls; hardening; dependencies; patching; backup and recovery; audit logging; monitoring; health; production protections.

capabilities.name: Security Risk Management
capabilities.purpose: Evaluate exposure and consequence separately from the threat scenarios that create them.
capabilities.scope: Risk register; description; affected assets; likelihood, impact, and severity; owner; mitigation; compensating controls; residual and accepted risk; expiry, review, evidence, and status.

capabilities.name: Security Exceptions
capabilities.purpose: Make every deviation explicit, owned, risk-assessed, approved, reviewable, and time-bounded.
capabilities.scope: Exception ID, affected control, rationale, requester, human approver, risk, compensating control, scope, start, expiry, review date, and status; no invisible permanent bypasses.

capabilities.name: Compliance / Framework Mapping
capabilities.purpose: Map external obligations to canonical Shield controls without making an external framework the internal source of truth.
capabilities.scope: Future mappings for ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF, CIS Controls, OWASP, SOC 2-style controls, and relevant regulation.

capabilities.name: Asset / Security Scope Awareness
capabilities.purpose: Associate security requirements and evidence with ecosystem assets without duplicating the canonical inventory.
capabilities.scope: References to repositories, applications, services, APIs, infrastructure, environments, databases, datasets, identities, secrets, and third-party dependencies.

capabilities.name: Data Security
capabilities.purpose: Make security requirements responsive to the classification and lifecycle of protected data.
capabilities.scope: Inventory, classification, ownership, sensitivity, confidentiality, integrity, availability, access, encryption, retention, deletion, backups, recovery, transfer, export, sharing, logging restrictions, test data, and lifecycle.

capabilities.name: Threat Modeling
capabilities.purpose: Describe how assets could be harmed and connect scenarios to mitigations, controls, risk, ownership, review, and evidence.
capabilities.scope: Assets, actors, entry points, trust boundaries, data flows, dependencies, attack surfaces, abuse cases, threat scenarios, mitigations, controls, residual or accepted risk, unresolved threats, owner, review date, evidence, and versions.

capabilities.name: Attack Surface Management
capabilities.purpose: Maintain a current view of reachable entry points, trust boundaries, and unexpected exposure.
capabilities.scope: External and internal endpoints, ports, ingress and egress, administrative interfaces, DNS, dependencies, trust boundaries, and production exposure.

capabilities.name: Third-Party / Dependency Security
capabilities.purpose: Understand and govern the security exposure created by suppliers, hosted services, and external APIs.
capabilities.scope: Third-party inventory, criticality, data access, trust level, requirements, security review, known risks, expiry, and reassessment.

capabilities.name: Strong Room
capabilities.purpose: Provide the implemented reusable security baseline for private applications while leaving populated configuration and deployment evidence with adopters.
capabilities.scope: Access and MFA; protected Tunnel ingress and JWT validation; NGINX; hardened Docker/Compose; health; logout; release and deployment security; direct-origin protection; production verification; security evidence.

capabilities.name: Identity & Access Management (IAM)
capabilities.purpose: Govern who and what may access ecosystem resources across human, service, and workload identities without vendor lock-in.
capabilities.scope: Authentication, authorization, RBAC and appropriate ABAC, least privilege, MFA/passkeys, privileged and administrative access, break glass, service-to-service access, requests and approvals, reviews, dormant accounts, joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle, temporary access, expiry, ownership, and audit trail.

capabilities.name: Secrets Management
capabilities.purpose: Govern secret material through inventory, secure storage, scoped use, rotation, revocation, and auditable access without storing secrets in the Shield.
capabilities.scope: Environment secrets, API keys, tokens, certificates, private keys, service and database credentials, encryption keys, classification, ownership, storage, rotation, expiry, revocation, emergency rotation, leakage detection, repository scanning, and CI/CD handling.

capabilities.name: Application Security
capabilities.purpose: Define secure development and runtime requirements for applications and APIs.
capabilities.scope: Input validation, output encoding, authentication, authorization, sessions, CSRF, CORS, headers, API security, rate limiting, abuse prevention, dependencies, errors, secure logging, uploads, SSRF, injection, threat models, testing, and production hardening.

capabilities.name: Network & Perimeter Security
capabilities.purpose: Govern trusted paths, exposure, isolation, and protected ingress/egress, with Strong Room as the private-application pattern rather than a competing model.
capabilities.scope: Ingress and egress, exposed services, direct-origin protection, trusted networks, tunnels, reverse proxies, firewalls, segmentation, isolation, administrative interfaces, external/internal endpoints, TLS and trust boundaries, DNS security, remote access, and production exposure.

capabilities.name: Secure Configuration & Hardening
capabilities.purpose: Define versioned secure baselines and validate deviations for systems and services.
capabilities.scope: Operating systems, containers, Docker/Compose, reverse proxies, networks, databases, cloud services, runtimes, endpoints, TLS, headers, ports, ingress, privileged execution, file permissions, and production configuration.

capabilities.name: Software Supply Chain Security
capabilities.purpose: Establish provenance and integrity from third-party dependency and source through build, artifact, and release.
capabilities.scope: Dependency provenance and vulnerabilities, lockfiles, package integrity, build provenance, artifact integrity, SBOMs, signing, attestations, trusted build systems, source-to-artifact traceability, third-party components, and release provenance.

capabilities.name: CI/CD & Deployment Security
capabilities.purpose: Separate technical validation from human production authorization while securing build and deployment paths.
capabilities.scope: Protected branches, PR reviews, automated security and required checks, deployment identities and authorization, environment protections, human production gates, artifact verification, immutable releases, rollback readiness, production SHA, post-deployment validation, and evidence.
expectedControls: human gate immediately before production impact

capabilities.name: Logging, Monitoring & Detection
capabilities.purpose: Define trustworthy security observability and alerting that fails visibly and can integrate with a future SIEM without vendor coupling.
capabilities.scope: Audit, authentication, authorization failure, privilege, configuration, deployment, secret access, suspicious activity, application and infrastructure events; centralization, normalization, retention, integrity, alerting, rules, severity, ownership, investigation, and coverage.

capabilities.name: Vulnerability Management
capabilities.purpose: Turn discovered vulnerabilities into owned, prioritized, time-bounded remediation and validated closure.
capabilities.scope: Discovery, inventory, severity, affected asset/repository/service, CVE, exploitability, remediation owner and status, SLA, exceptions, compensating controls, validation, and closure evidence.
futureAutomation: dependency, container, SAST, DAST, infrastructure and configuration scanner ingestion

capabilities.name: Security Testing
capabilities.purpose: Produce provenance-bearing evidence through automated and manual security validation.
capabilities.scope: SAST, DAST, dependency, secret, container, infrastructure, and configuration scanning; penetration, manual, adversarial, regression, production exposure, authentication, and authorization testing.

capabilities.name: Incident Response
capabilities.purpose: Govern the complete security incident lifecycle from detection through validated closure.
capabilities.scope: Detection, reporting, triage, classification, severity, ownership, escalation, containment, eradication, recovery, communications and notifications, evidence preservation, forensics, timeline, root cause, corrective actions, lessons, post-incident review, closure, and follow-up validation.

capabilities.name: Forensics / Evidence Preservation
capabilities.purpose: Preserve attributable, integrity-protected incident material while respecting sensitivity and authorization boundaries.
capabilities.scope: Forensic readiness, collection authority, chain of custody, source timestamps, integrity, retention, access, redaction, investigation links, and secure handoff.
expectedPolicies: Forensic Readiness and Evidence Preservation Policy

capabilities.name: Corrective Actions
capabilities.purpose: Convert incidents, findings, and reviews into owned fixes with validation and durable learning.
capabilities.scope: Action description, source incident/finding, owner, due date, priority, remediation, validation, residual risk, closure, and recurrence prevention.

capabilities.name: Business Continuity / Security Resilience
capabilities.purpose: Define the security properties of backup, recovery, emergency access, and restoration without taking operational ownership from infrastructure or service teams.
capabilities.scope: Backup security, restoration verification, disaster-recovery security, credential recovery, emergency access, service recovery, recovery dependencies, validation, and exercises.

capabilities.name: Security Controls
capabilities.purpose: Provide the canonical, machine-addressable abstraction for required safeguards, applicability, assessment, evidence, exceptions, and traceability.
capabilities.scope: Control ID, title, description, objective, applicability, mandatory/recommended designation, owner, guidance, validation method, evidence requirements, compliance state, exception, last checked, next review, and links to standards, risks, threats, assets, repositories, and services.

capabilities.name: Evidence & Assurance
capabilities.purpose: Make security evidence first-class and distinguish declarations from observations and verified claims.
capabilities.scope: Evidence item and source; generated timestamp; collection method; repository and commit; environment; artifact/version; control; result; confidence; provenance; reviewer; expiry and staleness.

capabilities.name: Maturity & Continuous Improvement
capabilities.purpose: Measure capability maturity honestly and drive recurring, evidence-based improvement.
capabilities.scope: Maturity assessment, control coverage and drift, recurring reviews, KPIs/KRIs, lessons, improvement backlog, reassessment, and transparent roadmap progress.
